Article Title: No MDR on UPI from October 15? Government considers delaying rollout of fees: Report
Article Text:
UPI will continue to be free for consumers, with no transaction fee imposed on person-to-person payments.

What is MDR on UPI ?

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you think the implementation of MDR will affect UPI transaction volumes? It will decrease significantly. It will stay about the same. It will increase, due to more merchants participating. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Will the rollout of Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface ( UPI ) transactions be deferred to January 2027? The government may postpone the move which was scheduled to be effective from October 15, 2026, by a few months, according to a regulatory official and an industry executive familiar with the matter.Last month, the government ended the zero-fee regime for UPI by allowing merchants to be charged 0.4% on transactions above Rs 2,000. UPI is used by more than 500 million people across the country for payments ranging from roadside cups of tea to iPhones.The charge is scheduled to take effect on October 15, coinciding with the annual festive season, which runs from October through December and usually brings a significant increase in consumer spending.Sources told Reuters that the proposed postponement would prevent any disruption to retail payments during the festive period while giving payments companies additional time to prepare their systems for the new fee.Investors had regarded the fee as an important monetisation opportunity for payments companies, which were expected to receive a share of the proceeds.Shares of Indian digital payments companies fell on Thursday following reports of the possible delay.Paytm dropped 7.6%, while One Mobikwik Systems declined 7.2%.Yesterday, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said that introducing a "small fee" through the MDR is unlikely to have a "major impact" on the volume of UPI transactions."As of now, we do not see any drop in volumes. And I don't personally think that a small fee will have a major impact on the volumes," he told reporters at the central bank's headquarters.MDR refers to the charge paid by a merchant when accepting payments for goods or services through credit or debit cards. It is generally calculated as a percentage of the transaction amount and is deducted by the bank before the merchant receives the payment.The government has clarified that UPI will continue to be free for consumers, with no transaction fee imposed on person-to-person payments.The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) notified an MDR of 0.4% for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 in September. Person-to-person payments will remain free. For transactions of Rs 75,000 or more, the MDR will be subject to a maximum charge of Rs 300 per transaction.Small-value UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000 will not be affected. These transactions account for more than 95% of the total volume of UPI P2M transactions.The objective behind introducing a reasonable MDR is to keep UPI accessible and convenient for everyday payments while also supporting the long-term sustainability of the UPI ecosystem.A gazette notification issued on September 14 specifies that banks and system providers cannot levy any fee, whether directly or indirectly, on individuals making or receiving payments through RuPay debit cards or UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000.The notification follows an amendment to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, which established a framework allowing Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) to be imposed on payments made through UPI and other electronic payment methods notified under the law.Parliament approved the amendment Bill during the Monsoon Session in August this year.
Article Summary: The government may postpone the move which was scheduled to be effective from October 15, 2026, by a few months. Last month, the government ended the zero-fee regime for UPI by allowing merchants to be charged 0.4% on transactions above Rs 2,000. The charge is scheduled to take effect on October 15.

Article Title: AI regulation consultation paper next month, says IT minister Vaishnaw; focus on safety, deepfakes
Article Text:
Vaishnaw said the government had reached a stage where India needed a regulatory framework for AI, but stressed that legislation alone would not be enough.

Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Friday said that government is working on bringing AI regulations starting with releasing a Consultation paper next month.The paper will focus on AI safety, harms arising from its use, deepfakes, a human-first approach and skilling, Vaishnaw said while speaking at an event on the release of the World Development Report.The minister said the government would release the regulation-focused consultation paper within a month, following which it would proceed with framing the AI regulatory framework.He said the government has now reached a stage where India needs a regulatory framework for AI, but stressed that legislation alone would not be enough. “We have to bring a techno-legal solution,” the minister said, adding that all stakeholders would need to be brought on board, as quoted by PTI.Vaishnaw said AI safety would be the most important focus of the consultation paper. He also flagged the growing sophistication of deepfakes, calling them a “nuisance which can cause huge problems in society”.“People believe them, and it sets a totally wrong precedent. It sets a totally wrong narrative, and people get lured into doing wrong things and believing wrong things,” he said.The minister added that the framework would also address AI-related harms, including cybersecurity, user harm and psychological disorders, while ensuring that people are not left behind as the technology develops.He further said the industry would have to shoulder the primary responsibility for addressing these risks, including safety, cybersecurity, user harms and deepfakes.“Humanity has to be the most important part of change that has happened,” Vaishnaw said, adding that the consultation paper would include a commitment to skilling.This comes about two months after the government tightened IT Rules for social media platforms and other online intermediaries to tackle AI-generated deepfakes and other synthetically generated content, including deepfakes, child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate images and AI-based impersonation.The amendments also cut the deadline for removing unlawful content from 36 hours to three hours after a valid government or court notice, while requiring significant social media intermediaries to use automated tools to proactively detect certain unlawful material and address sensitive complaints, such as nudity and impersonation, within two hours. Failure to comply can result in platforms losing their safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act.
Article Summary: The paper will focus on AI safety, harms arising from its use, deepfakes, a human-first approach and skilling. Vaishnaw said the government would release the regulation-focused consultation paper within a month, following which it would proceed with framing the AI regulatory framework.

Article Text:

Seven New High-Speed Rail Corridors: Key Details

India’s first bullet train

Imagine travelling from Delhi to Varanasi by train in less than 4 hours, or even covering the distance between Mumbai and Pune in less than an hour! In the coming years, Indian Railways is looking to make that a reality with seven new bullet train corridors in the works.Earlier this year, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced seven new high-speed rail corridors in her Union Budget speech.The announcement comes as Indian Railways is already seeking to transform overnight travel with the introduction of Vande Bharat sleeper trains, designed to provide faster journeys with a more world-class, passenger-centric experience.While presenting the Budget, the Finance Minister announced, “In order to promote environmentally sustainable passenger systems, we will develop seven High-Speed Rail corridors between cities as ‘growth connectors.”Also Read | Second Vande Bharat sleeper set to launch this month between Bengaluru and Mumbai; cutting travel time from 24 hours to under 16 hours, 30 year wait for faster connectivity between two cities to end What will make these train corridors special is that India is taking a manufacturing leap as well by making its own bullet trains for the first time.So, which seven routes have been selected for the new high-speed rail corridors, and how much could journey times be reduced?The proposed corridor will connect the national capital with eastern Uttar Pradesh, reducing the journey to around 3 hours 50 minutes.It is intended to improve tourism connectivity, connect secondary cities and support the development of an economic belt extending across Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal.The flagship corridor in the western region will connect two major urban centres, bringing the journey time down to just 48 minutes.Along with upgrades to congested trunk routes and suburban rail services, the project is aimed at meeting the state’s rising passenger and freight requirements.The corridor will connect Maharashtra and Telangana, with the journey expected to take about 1 hour 55 minutes.It will form part of a broader high-speed connection across western and southern India, offering passengers faster and more dependable connectivity while supporting regional economies.This route is part of the emerging southern high-speed rail “diamond” and is expected to cut travel time to around 2 hours.The faster connection will improve mobility between major IT, manufacturing and service centres in Karnataka and Telangana.The journey between these two southern economic centres is expected to take approximately 2 hours 55 minutes.The corridor is expected to support business activity, movement of talent and inter-state commuting across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry.The corridor is expected to bring travel time down to about 1 hour 13 minutes. It will further expand the high-speed rail network in southern India while strengthening connectivity between major cities and the regions around them.Travel between Varanasi and Siliguri via Patna is expected to take around 2 hours 55 minutes.The corridor will connect important religious, educational and medical centres across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal. It will also mark the first high-speed rail service in eastern India, widening opportunities for trade, services and inter-regional mobility.Also Read | Vande Bharat crosses world’s highest Chenab and first cable-stayed Anji bridges at 100 kmph in historic milestone as Katra-Banihal speed limit rises over a year after inauguration India is also developing its first bullet train corridor between Ahmedabad and Mumbai, with the initial section expected to become operational in the coming years. Bullet trains typically operate at speeds of around 300 kmph, while some definitions of high-speed rail cover services operating at around 220-250 kmph.Indian Railways is looking to open a section of its first bullet train corridor. While the entire Mumbai-Ahmedabad stretch will still take a few more years, a small stretch in Gujarat is likely to be thrown open by August 2027.Two high-speed trains are currently being manufactured by BEML and are expected to roll out for testing in the first half of 2027.
Article Summary: Seven new high-speed rail corridors have been announced by Indian Railways. Journey times between Delhi and Varanasi expected to be cut from 4 hours to just 3 hours 50 minutes. India is also developing its first bullet train corridor between Ahmedabad and Mumbai. Bullet trains typically operate at speeds of around 300 kmph.

Article Title: New breast cancer drug moves closer to India
Article Text:
Camizestrant, a new breast cancer drug shown to delay disease progression in patients with ESR1 mutations, has been recommended for import and marketing in India

NEW DELHI: A new breast cancer drug that can help delay the disease from worsening has moved closer to India. Camizestrant, already approved in the US, European Union , UAE and Saudi Arabia, has been recommended for import and marketing in India by a government expert panel.In a major trial, patients who switched to the drug after a change was detected in their cancer cells remained free of worsening disease for 16 months on average, compared with 9.2 months among those who continued their earlier treatment. The trial involved 315 patients and found a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.The drug is meant for adults with a common type of advanced breast cancer whose treatment has started losing effectiveness. An ESR1 mutation, which can develop during hormone treatment, can make the cancer resistant to the treatment being used.“Camizestrant could be an important new option for Indian patients with advanced breast cancer who develop an ESR1 resistance mutation during hormone treatment. A blood test can detect the mutation before the disease visibly worsens, allowing treatment to be changed earlier and potentially delaying chemotherapy,” said Dr Pragya Shukla, head of clinical oncology, Delhi State Cancer Institute.She said the bigger challenge would be making ESR1 testing affordable and accessible, particularly for patients outside major cancer centres.The recommendation was made by the Subject Expert Committee (Oncology) at its meeting at the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) headquarters on September 22. The panel noted that camizestrant addressed an unmet medical need and recommended a waiver of the local Phase III trial requirement.If ultimately approved in India, camizestrant will be available only on prescription from a medical oncologist. The company has also been asked to conduct a Phase IV clinical trial and submit its protocol to CDSCO within three months of approval.The US Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval to camizestrant on September 4, 2026, based on the SERENA-6 trial. The FDA approval also carries warnings about irregular heart rhythm, slow heart rate and potential harm to an unborn baby.The September 22 oncology meeting also reviewed other cancer treatments. The panel sought additional safety data for an under-the-skin form of amivantamab for certain advanced lung cancers, permitted a Phase IV trial of durvalumab in Indian patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer, and approved a revised Phase IV trial of lutetium Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan with at least 80 patients. It did not waive the Phase III trial requirement for trilaciclib, citing lack of unmet need, Indian patient data and comparative evidence.
Article Summary: Camizestrant is already approved in the US, European Union, UAE and Saudi Arabia. The drug is meant for adults with a common type of advanced breast cancer. An ESR1 mutation, which can develop during hormone treatment, can make the cancer resistant to the treatment being used.

Article Title: Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemption
Article Text:
A CBDT Notification No. 31/2023 dated 24 May 2023 increased the exemption limit for non-government employees from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 25 lakh. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did ITAT rule in favour of the retired employee?

Significance for taxpayers

You retire and get leave encashment, a part of which is exempt from tax. You file your income tax return claiming the exemption, but later the exemption limit is hiked. Are you entitled to the benefits of the enhanced leave encashment exemption limit?In one such case, the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Chennai has given its decision in favour of a retired bank employee.The case involved a question that has come up before several tax tribunals: whether the higher leave-encashment exemption introduced in 2023 can also benefit employees who retired before that change, particularly when their tax proceedings were still being pursued.The taxpayer had retired from a bank during the financial year 2019-20. On superannuation, he received Rs 12,27,232 as leave encashment.When he filed his income tax return for assessment year 2020-21 on September 10, 2020, he claimed Rs 3 lakh as exempt under Section 10(10AA)(ii) of the Income Tax Act. After claiming that exemption, he declared a total income of Rs 24,36,260.Also Read | US-based daughter files case against parents seeking share in properties; Karnataka HC rejects her ‘ancestral’ claim, saying they were father's separate assets, not coparcenary property At that time, the exemption ceiling for leave encashment applicable to non-government employees was Rs 3 lakh. The man accordingly claimed exemption of Rs 3 lakh when he filed his income tax return.Subsequently, a CBDT Notification No. 31/2023 dated 24 May 2023 increased the exemption limit for non-government employees from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 25 lakh.The notification stated that it would come into force from 1 April 2023, while its Explanatory Memorandum records that no person would be adversely affected by giving retrospective effect to the notification.That change prompted the man to seek the benefit of the higher exemption against his earlier claim. Since he had received only Rs 12.27 lakh, he sought exemption for the entire amount, rather than the Rs 3 lakh he had originally claimed.His return had already been processed by the Centralised Processing Centre (CPC), Bengaluru, under Section 143(1) on December 13, 2020. The CPC had allowed the Rs 3 lakh exemption and brought the balance leave encashment to tax.The man subsequently appealed against the CPC's order before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) on January 7, 2026. The CIT(A), however, rejected his claim on February 25, 2026. It held that the notification applicable to assessment year 2020-21 was the earlier notification that prescribed the Rs 3 lakh ceiling.The man then approached the Chennai ITAT.Also Read | Man deposits Rs 85.3 lakh received as cash gifts from wife, relatives; income tax calls it unexplained and sends notice, but ITAT Chennai accepts gift deeds and gives relief The key question before the ITAT was whether the enhanced limit could benefit an employee who had retired before 1 April 2023. The Tribunal answered this in the affirmative.Before ITAT, it was argued that the 2023 enhancement was beneficial and curative. Although the notification specified April 1, 2023 as its effective date, the taxpayer argued that its explanatory memorandum and the nature of the amendment supported its application to his case.The Tribunal began by identifying the central issue: whether the man was entitled to exemption up to Rs 25 lakh under Section 10(10AA)(ii), or whether the exemption for his assessment year had to remain restricted to Rs 3 lakh.The bench noted that Section 10(10AA)(ii) already provided an exemption for leave encashment received by non-government employees, subject to a monetary ceiling notified by the Central Government.According to Amit Ganatra, Executive Director, Khaitan & Co, ITAT’s reasoning was principally founded on the beneficial and remedial character of the CBDT notification.“The ITAT noted that the notification did not create a new exemption or introduce a new class of eligible taxpayers; rather, it enhanced the monetary ceiling of an exemption which was already available to non-government employees under section 10(10AA)(ii),” Ganatra tells TOI.Also Read | 83-year-old woman got Rs 12.28 lakh after son’s death, but sought Rs 15,000 maintenance from college-going granddaughter and a share of family pension from son’s widow; Kerala HC rejects both claims The earlier ceiling of Rs 3 lakh had remained unchanged for almost 20 years, despite substantial changes in salary levels and the economic environment.“ITAT therefore viewed the enhancement to Rs 25 lakh as a measure intended to update and rationalise an existing provision and to mitigate the hardship arising from the continued application of an outdated monetary limit. ITAT also considered it inequitable to deny the benefit of the enhanced ceiling to employees merely because their retirement preceded the date on which the notification was issued, particularly where the benefit was otherwise intended to address the inadequacy of the earlier limit,” he said.A significant factor considered by the ITAT was the Explanatory Memorandum accompanying Notification No. 31/2023. While the notification itself provides that it shall come into force from 1 April 2023, the Explanatory Memorandum specifically states that “no person is being adversely affected by giving retrospective effect to the notification”.ITAT held that provisions intended to confer a benefit and remove hardship should be interpreted liberally and, in appropriate cases, applied retrospectively, particularly where doing so did not adversely affect any vested right of the Revenue.The bench also said the absence of an express retrospective clause could not by itself settle the issue when the amendment merely enlarged an existing benefit. In its view, the remedial nature of the change had to be considered.Ganatra explained that ITAT relied on this to ascertain the remedial intent underlying the enhancement. In such circumstances, the absence of an express provision giving retrospective effect was not considered determinative, particularly since the notification merely enlarged the monetary limit of an existing exemption.ITAT also noted the settled judicial principle that beneficial and curative amendments may be applied in appropriate cases to advance the cause of justice.Ganatra says that another important factor was the judicial consistency emerging from various ITAT benches.“The Chennai Bench referred to a number of earlier decisions which had similarly allowed the enhanced Rs 25 lakh limit in cases involving earlier retirement years. ITAT therefore considered its conclusion to be supported by a developing line of coordinate-bench decisions,” he said.After considering the statutory provision, the notification, the explanatory material and the earlier ITAT decisions, the Chennai ITAT held that the man was entitled to the enhanced Rs 25 lakh limit.Because his leave encashment was Rs 12,27,232, the entire amount was below the enhanced ceiling and therefore eligible for exemption.The Tribunal consequently set aside the restriction imposed by the CPC and the order of the CIT(A). It directed the Assessing Officer to allow the exemption claimed by the man.Also Read | Man opted for VRS after employer shut plant, got Rs 65.21 lakh and reported it as advance salary in ITR; Section 89 relief was denied, but ITAT Pune later ruled it a non-taxable capital receipt The Khaitan & Co expert says that for taxpayers, the ruling is particularly relevant to non-government employees who retired before 1 April 2023 and whose exemption for leave encashment was restricted to Rs 3 lakh.“The decision provides judicial support for the position that the enhanced exemption limit of Rs 25 lakh may also be available in respect of such earlier years,” he says.However, he cautions that the issue is not free from judicial divergence.“In Purnendu Shekhar Sinha v. Union of India, the Patna High Court, while examining the constitutional validity of the distinction under section 10(10AA) between employees of the Central/State Governments and employees of other establishments, held that such classification was not discriminatory and proceeded on the basis that 1 April 2023 is the operative date for the enhanced exemption limit,” he says.“This judgement was not brought to the notice of the Chennai ITAT. Accordingly, while the Chennai ITAT ruling strengthens the case for retrospective application of the enhanced limit, the issue cannot, at this stage, be regarded as conclusively settled for all taxpayers,” he adds.
Article Summary: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Chennai has given its decision in favour of a retired bank employee. The case involved a question that has come up before several tax tribunals. The key question before the ITAT was whether the enhanced limit could benefit an employee who had retired before 1 April 2023. The Tribunal answered this in the affirmative.

Article Title: When support matters most: How Policybazaar helps customers navigate medical emergencies
Article Text:
Racing against time for a cancer patient

Prakash Dixit

Going beyond paperwork during a stroke emergency

Subhash Yadav

Correcting one medical detail saved a Rs 20 lakh claim

Sayyed Hussain

Standing by customers beyond the policy purchase

References:

The article has been contributed by Amit Chhabra, Chief Business Officer, General Insurance, Policybazaar.

Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.

Buying a good comprehensive health insurance policy is just the start. The real test comes during a medical emergency, when families face hospital chaos, treatment decisions, procedural red tape, and the clock ticking on your finances. That’s where most policyholders are left scrambling alone.Not at Policybazaar.In FY26, Policybazaar navigated over 3.75 lakh insurance claims, including more than 2.45 lakh health insurance claims, serving as the crucial bridge between patients and payouts. Every single day, its specialized claims team fields more than 7,000 interactions: documentation handholding, hospital negotiations, relentless follow-throughs. Not only that, Policybazaar successfully intervened to get 11,156 rejected health insurance claims reconsidered and paid out over the past year, working closely with our insurance partners.Because Policybazaar’s support at the ‘moment of truth’ is what sets us apart, especially when families need guidance and timely assistance during a claim. When hospitals won't wait. When TPAs demand more documents. That's when timely expertise, domain knowledge, and sheer persistence become the difference between financial catastrophe and recovery.When Policybazaar customerreached out in March 2026, he was deeply distressed. His mother's chemotherapy claim had been rejected because the insurer was unable to establish the duration of her illness.The situation was urgent. Her next chemotherapy session was scheduled within six days, with each treatment costing nearly Rs 80,000. Delaying treatment was not an option, while paying for it themselves was beyond the family's means.Policybazaar's claims team immediately began reviewing the medical records to understand why the claim had been declined. During the review, they identified an earlier consultation that established the timeline of the illness, an important medical detail that had not been adequately considered during the initial assessment. Armed with this evidence, the team escalated the case to the insurer's medical panel and requested an expedited review, given the patient's next chemotherapy session was only days away.Within hours, the insurer partner completed a fresh assessment, approved the claim in full and also cleared future chemotherapy treatments. For the family, the outcome meant they could focus on recovery instead of worrying about arranging funds."At a time when we were only thinking about my mother's treatment, the Policybazaar team took ownership of everything else. We will always be grateful for the support," Dixit later shared with the team.Forand his wife,, the crisis came unexpectedly.Just months after porting their health insurance policy through Policybazaar , Yadav suffered a severe brain stroke and was rushed to Kailash Hospital, Noida, where he was diagnosed with a subdural haemorrhage. When the hospital raised a cashless request, the insurer declined it, citing concerns over a possible undisclosed medical history because the policy had recently been ported.Despite repeated clarifications from the hospital and treating doctors, the claim continued to be denied.When the family approached Policybazaar, the company's medical panel reviewed every clinical document to understand the insurer partner's concerns and pinpointed the precise evidence required to address them. Rather than leaving the family to gather the paperwork themselves, a Policybazaar representative visited the hospital, worked alongside the treating team and hospital administration, collected the missing clinical records and ensured the insurer received a complete medical submission.Once the additional information was submitted, our insurance partner reassessed the case and approved the cashless claim. The approval meant the family could concentrate on his treatment instead of worrying about arranging funds during an already stressful time."We had almost given up hope. The Policybazaar team stayed with us through the process until the approval finally came," recalled Anu Yadav.Another case involved, a 34-year-old customer who was hospitalised with kidney failure and also suffered a heart attack within a year of purchasing his health insurance policy.The estimated treatment cost was around Rs 20 lakh. However, the insurer initially rejected the claim because the duration of his chronic kidney disease had been incorrectly recorded by the treating doctor.When Hussain's sister approached Policybazaar for help, the claims team immediately stepped in. Instead of accepting the rejection at face value, the team reconstructed the patient's medical history from the available records. During this review, they discovered that the duration of the illness had been incorrectly recorded in the medical documents. The first consultation letter clearly established that the diagnosis had actually been made after the policy was issued, fundamentally changing the insurer's assessment of the claim.Armed with this medical evidence, Policybazaar escalated the matter with the insurer and remained closely engaged until the case was reassessed. Following a detailed review, the insurer approved the claim, covering multiple hospitalisations worth nearly Rs 20 lakh."Knowing someone was fighting for us during such a difficult time meant everything," Hussain's sister later told the Policybazaar team after his recovery.For most people, buying health insurance is a one-time decision. But the real experience begins when a claim has to be made.These are just a few of the many instances where Policybazaar stood by its customers and helped them navigate challenging situations. It often requires careful scrutiny of medical records, timely intervention, close engagement with hospitals and insurers, and persistent follow-through until a genuine claim reaches a fair outcome. While claim decisions remain with insurers and are subject to policy terms and conditions, timely intervention and accurate documentation can often make a meaningful difference.Behind every claim is a family looking for reassurance during a difficult time. These stories reflect Policybazaar's commitment to standing by its customers long after the policy has been purchased, helping them navigate one of life's most stressful moments with confidence and care.
Article Summary: In FY26, Policybazaar navigated over 3.75 lakh insurance claims, including more than 2.45 lakh health insurance claims. Every single day, its specialized claims team fields more than 7,000 interactions: documentation handholding, hospital negotiations, relentless follow-through.

Article Title: 'India's regulatory framework non-discriminatory,' govt responds to Musk
Article Text:
India refutes Elon Musk’s 'oligarch' allegation

NEW DELHI: India has rejected Elon Musk’s allegation that Starlink is being “being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. ” Govt said in a statement Thursday that “India's regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory” and that “the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived.”Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Starlink are the three entities plan to start satellite communication services in India. “Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all the three licensees. As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage,” govt statement added.Musk had on Wednesday said on X: “We are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are… This is a crime against the people of India!”The statement came on a day when Lauren Dreyer, VP of Starlink Business Operations, said at the India Mobile Congress that “We stand ready to serve India, as soon as India is ready.”“For years we have been setting the foundation for the same type of relationship (that Starlink has in countries were it operates) here in India, establishing MoUs with Jio, Airtel and more; working closely with state Govts to listen and learn how Starlink might be able to best serve once it is authorised,” she said at IMC.“Starlink can help reach places where the last mile is still the hardest mile, working alongside India’s operators, govt and industry. As India works through the final approvals, our message is simple: We stand ready to serve India, as soon as India is ready,” Dreyer added.Starlink has tried to allay India’s security fears by claiming that Indian user data will be kept in the country and having security controls as per the country’s requirement.Given strained India-US ties over multiple issues like the stuck trade deal, threat of tariffs over buying Russian oil and most importantly security concerns over Starlink, people in the know say Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Jio are likely to get the nod before Musk, whose wait could be much longer.
Article Summary: Starlink has tried to allay India’s security fears by claiming that Indian user data will be kept in the country. People in the know say Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio are likely to get the nod before Musk.

Article Title: CBSE Class 10, 12 private exam forms 2027 out: Apply online from today, check fees and important dates
Article Text:
CBSE Class 10, 12 private exam forms 2027 out

Who can apply for CBSE Class 10 private exam 2027?

Who can apply for CBSE Class 12 private exam 2027?

CBSE private exam form 2027 : Important dates

Event Class 10 Class 12 Application starts October 8, 2026 October 8, 2026 Last date without late fee October 23, 2026 October 23, 2026 Late fee window October 24 to 30, 2026 October 24 to 30, 2026 Examination February/March/April 2027 February/March/April 2027

CBSE Class 10 private exam fee

CBSE Class 12 private exam fee

How to apply for CBSE private exam 2027

Important instructions for candidates

The Central Board of Secondary Education ( CBSE ) has released the private candidate examination forms for Class 10 and Class 12 for the 2026-27 session. Eligible candidates can now submit their forms online through the CBSE website.The application process for both Class 10 and Class 12 private candidates has started today, October 8, 2026. Candidates can submit the form without a late fee till October 23, 2026. The late fee window will be open from October 24 to October 30.The forms are meant for the examination to be held in February/March/April 2027 along with the Board's main examinations 2027.According to the Class 10 notice, the form is open to certain categories of private candidates. These include students who were declared essential repeat in the 2026 examination, candidates placed in compartment in the 2026 examination, candidates declared fail or essential repeat in earlier examinations, and candidates who have passed the examination and want to appear for improving their performance in one or more subjects.The detailed eligibility conditions are given in the notice. For example, candidates placed in compartment in two subjects in 2026 have to select the category carefully while applying. The board has also specified separate conditions for candidates applying under improvement of performance. Read the official notice here. For Class 12, eligible categories include candidates declared essential repeat in the 2026 Senior School Certificate Examination, candidates placed in compartment in the 2026 examination, candidates declared fail or essential repeat in earlier examinations, and candidates who have passed and want to improve their performance in one or more subjects. SUBMISSION_FORMS_PRIVATE_XII_26…Candidates who completed a regular course of studies and were allotted a roll number for appearing in the 2026 examination can also fall under the eligibility conditions mentioned in the notice. The board has also specified conditions for candidates placed in compartment in one subject in the 2026 examination. Read the official notice here. Here's a look at the key dates:The Class 10 and Class 12 notices both state that applications will be accepted only online and as per the given schedule.Applications submitted after the last date will not be accepted.For Class 10 candidates in India, the examination fee is ₹320 per subject. Candidates in Nepal have to pay ₹1,100 per subject, while candidates in other countries have to pay ₹2,200 per subject.Candidates submitting the form during the late fee period will have to pay an additional late fee of ₹2,000.For Class 12 candidates in India, the examination fee is ₹320 per subject. The fee is ₹1,100 per subject for candidates in Nepal and ₹2,200 per subject for candidates in other countries.For Class 12 practical subjects, an additional practical fee applies. The fee is ₹160 per practical subject for candidates in India, ₹174 per practical subject for candidates in Nepal and ₹375 per practical subject for candidates in other countries.A late fee of ₹2,000 per candidate will be charged during the late submission period.Candidates need to submit the application form online through the CBSE website. The board has clearly stated that no offline application will be accepted.Candidates should first check their eligibility and then fill in the required details carefully. They will also have to upload their photograph and signature as per the instructions. The scanned JPG files of the photograph and signature should not exceed 40 KB.The examination fee has to be paid online through the payment methods allowed by CBSE. Candidates should use their own account or debit or credit card for payment and keep the payment details safely.Candidates should submit only one application form. They must provide a working email ID for One-Time Password (OTP) verification. The board has also advised candidates to enter their roll number, school number and examination centre number correctly.The examination centre allotted to a candidate will be final. No request for a change of examination centre will be considered after allotment. Candidates should therefore fill in their preferred city carefully while submitting the form.CBSE has also advised candidates to check all details before submitting the application. Once the form is submitted and the fee is paid, corrections may not be possible after the last date.Candidates can access the private candidate application through the CBSE website and should read the detailed instructions before submitting the form.
Article Summary: CBSE has released the private candidate examination forms for Class 10 and Class 12 for the 2026-27 session. Eligible candidates can now submit their forms online through the CBSE website. Candidates can submit the form without a late fee till October 23, 2026. Article Title: Iraq’s dinar takes a hit as official rate resets, market rate crosses 1,700
Article Text:
Iraq devalues its currency

Iraq’s dinar has taken a step down against the US dollar, with the country officially resetting its exchange rate from around 1,300 dinars to 1,500 dinars per dollar. But in the market, the dollar is already fetching more than 1,700 dinars.The new official rate was decided at a Cabinet meeting on Tuesday night, according to Iraq’s central bank, which said the move was made “to meet the relevant financial, economic and monetary requirements.”The previous official exchange rate had been set in 2023. In practice, however, Iraq has always had a difference between the official rate and the rate used by exchange shops. That gap had widened in recent months, with the unofficial rate crossing 1,600 dinars to the dollar even before the official devaluation.After the new official rate was announced, the market rate climbed further to more than 1,700 dinars per dollar.The widening gap has come amid the US-Iran war, which has at times spilled over into Iraq, and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Iraq’s economy relies heavily on oil exports, most of which were shipped through the strait before the war. Since the war began, Iraq has shifted to sending oil overland through Syria for export, a route that is more expensive and less efficient.Under the new official rate, Iraq’s Finance Ministry will sell dollars at 1,500 dinars per dollar, while consumers buying dollars from banks will pay 1,520 dinars per dollar.
Article Summary: Iraq devalues its dinar against the US dollar. The new official rate is 1,500 dinars per dollar. But in the market, the dollar is already fetching more than 1,700 dinars. The widening gap has come amid the US-Iran war and disruptions to shipping.

Article Title: Amazon Prime becomes 'permanent home' for Emmy Awards as 'Wheel Deal' system ends
Article Text:
Emmys shift from 'Wheel Deal' to Amazon Prime

The Emmys are leaving their decades-old broadcast TV rotation behind, with Amazon’s Prime Video set to become the awards show’s exclusive global streaming home from 2027.The Television Academy and Amazon announced a six-year agreement on Tuesday that will make the ceremony available live and free to audiences in more than 240 countries and territories. Furthermore, viewers will not need a Prime Video subscription to watch the show.The ceremony will continue to take place in September, with Prime Video’s rights beginning with the 2027 edition. NBC, owned by Comcast, aired this year’s ceremony on September 14.The deal brings an end to the “Wheel Deal” system under which ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC took turns broadcasting the Emmys. The arrangement has been in place since at least 1994, with the latest eight-year contract expiring this year.Prime Video has been named the “permanent home” of the Emmys in the announcement, marking a departure from the awards show’s long-running practice of moving between the four US broadcast networks.“Television has never been more global, and the Emmys should be a celebration that the world can share,” Television Academy chair Cris Abrego said in a statement.“Having a dedicated home with Prime Video allows us to build on that legacy with unprecedented global reach and a broader commitment to the Television Academy and our mission throughout the year,” he said.The financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed.The move comes as streaming services take a larger role in live television, while traditional broadcast and cable networks face increasing competition as viewing habits shift towards streaming subscriptions. Major entertainment and sports events have increasingly moved to or added streaming platforms, including events whose rights were previously held exclusively by traditional networks.The Emmys' move is also part of a wider shift among major US awards shows. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced in December 2025 that Alphabet’s YouTube and YouTube TV would take over media rights to the Oscars from ABC in 2029. Netflix has exclusively aired the SAG Awards since 2024.For Amazon, the agreement adds a major live entertainment event to Prime Video’s existing offering of original films and television programmes, sports and other streaming partnerships.First held in 1949, the Emmy Awards recognise achievements in television acting, production and writing, among other categories. The ceremony has traditionally been a major promotional and cultural event for the US television industry.
Article Summary: The Emmys are leaving their decades-old broadcast TV rotation behind. Amazon's Prime Video will become the awards show's exclusive global streaming home from 2027. The deal brings an end to the “Wheel Deal’ system under which ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC took turns broadcasting the Emmys.

Article Title: Brent crosses $101 as Saudi attacks, US storm add to oil supply concerns
Article Text:
Brent crosses $101 once again

Oil prices rose more than 1% on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing the $101-a-barrel mark as fresh supply risks outweighed rising optimism due to increased Middle East crude supplies.WTI crude rose 1.05% to $90.38 a barrel, while Brent crude gained 1.02% to $101.60 as supply concerns emerged in Saudi Arabia and the US oil and refining sector.The latest concerns came from both sides of the global oil supply chain. According to US forecasters, a storm developing in the Gulf of Mexico is expected to become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days and is likely to affect oil and gas facilities.The areas in the storm's path account for 15% of US crude production and 5% of the country's natural gas production. Six refineries could also be affected. Refineries located in US Gulf states represent about 50% of the country's total refining capacity of 18.2 million barrels per day (bpd).The prospect of disruption has emerged even as oil supplies from the Middle East have increased. Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman on Tuesday said that supply had been rising, with the East-West pipeline reaching 5.8 million barrels a day.The head of Vitol said that around 12 million barrels per day of crude oil and 2 million bpd of refined products had been shipped out of the Middle East by tankers over the previous seven to 10 days.US inventory data, however, offered a mixed picture. According to market sources citing by Reuters, crude and gasoline inventories declined last week, while distillate stocks increased marginally. US crude inventories fell by 2.09 million barrels in the week ended October 2.Meanwhile, tensions around Saudi Arabia have added another risk to regional supply. The Saudi aviation authority said airports in Jazan and Najran were attacked twice on Monday evening as hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis escalated.The attacks came as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces pursued a major offensive to regain territory from the Houthis after weeks of rebel advances. Saudi Arabia has increased airstrikes in support of the campaign.Mukesh Sahdev, chief oil analyst at X Analysts in Sydney, said the attacks and refinery outages could continue to support higher oil prices.“Attacks and refinery outages are likely to keep the cracks elevated and scarcity will transmit to crude. Prices will stay elevated near a $100 level without any material de-escalation emerging,” Sahdev said.The wider tensions involving Iran have also remained unresolved. US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that there was uncertainty over who was running Iran during the eight-month US-Israeli war with Iran."Their leaders are gone, their second group of leaders are gone, and the biggest problem I have is nobody knows who the hell is running the country," Trump said.Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said on Sunday that Washington knows very well who its counterpart is in Iran and how the decision-making system in the country works.
Article Summary: WTI crude rose 1.05% to $90.38 a barrel, while Brent crude gained 1.02% to £101.60. Fresh supply concerns emerged in Saudi Arabia and the US oil and refining sector. A storm developing in the Gulf of Mexico is expected to become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days.

Article Title: Wall Street today: US stocks nears record highs amid earnings optimism, tech rally; S&P, Nasdaq rise 0.8%
Article Text:
Dow, S&P, Nasdaq rise to near record highs

Software stocks stage a comeback

US stocks moved closer to record highs on Tuesday, helped by stronger earnings expectations, easing oil prices and a renewed rally in technology shares.The S&P 500 rose 0.8 per cent and was on course to close above its previous record set in August. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 343 points, or 0.7 per cent, while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.8%, moving towards a fresh record after reaching an all-time high a day earlier.The gains have come despite continued concerns over inflation, elevated bond yields and the economic impact of the war with Iran. The S&P 500 has risen nearly 24% since hitting its low in late March.A key support for the rally has been expectations of stronger corporate profits. Analysts expect companies in the S&P 500 to report nearly 30% growth in earnings per share for the July-September quarter, according to FactSet. If realised, it would mark the third consecutive quarter in which earnings growth exceeded 25%.The easing in oil prices also provided some relief. Brent crude fell 1.1% to $99.19 a barrel, down from nearly $110 a few weeks ago. The decline helped push the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note down to 5.26%, from 5.31% on Monday.US software stocks have emerged as another driver of the market's recent strength, with investors increasingly betting that artificial intelligence will help rather than destroy demand for many software companies.The S&P 500 software and services index rose 1.3 per cent on Tuesday to its highest level since November 2025. The index also recorded its strongest quarterly gain since the second quarter of 2020 during the July-September period.Companies including Salesforce, ServiceNow and Accenture have reported strong results, while partnerships with AI companies have helped improve sentiment towards the sector. Cybersecurity stocks have performed particularly strongly as businesses increase spending to protect systems in the age of AI.CrowdStrike, Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks have all recorded triple-digit gains this year.“AI has been more of an enabler for a lot of these software companies, more than a disruptor,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist at LPL Financial.The software index is up about 5% this year, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has surged 87.5%, although chip stocks have pulled back from their highs. Meanwhile, expectations for software-sector earnings growth in 2026 have climbed to 20.6%, from 13.8% at the end of March, according to LSEG data.Software stocks suffered a sharp selloff earlier this year, with the sector falling more than 26% from late January to its April low. The decline was driven by fears that companies could use AI to develop software internally at a much lower cost, threatening traditional software providers.Those concerns now appear to have eased as companies report continued demand and greater adoption of AI tools.“The whole SaaSpocalypse didn't happen anywhere near as fast as some of the people on Wall Street thought it would,” said Rebecca Wettemann, CEO of technology research firm Valoir.However, analysts warn that AI remains a longer-term risk for the industry. Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, said the more significant test for software companies could come in the second half of 2027, when greater data-centre capacity could make AI-powered coding a bigger challenge for traditional software businesses.Additionallly, several major companies are due to report results in the coming days. Delta Air Lines is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on Friday, followed by several major US banks next week.In overseas markets, European stocks edged higher as investors continued to monitor government debt and bond yields. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 1.1%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 1%, while South Korea's Kospi fell 0.9%.
Article Summary: S&P 500 rose 0.8% and was on course to close above its previous record. Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 343 points, or 0.7%. Nasdaq Composite added 0. 8%, moving towards a fresh record. Gains come despite continued concerns over inflation, elevated bond yields and the economic impact of the war with Iran.

Article Title: Fueling both sides? South Korea ships 150,000T fuel to Russia while funding Ukraine
Article Text:
South Korea ships 150,000 tonnes fuel to Russia while funding Ukraine

Three sanctioned tankers sail to Russia

Russia turns to import fuel

South Korea is backing Ukraine, but its fuel tankers are sailing in the opposite direction — towards Russia.In July and August, more than 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mainly diesel, was shipped from South Korea to Russia as Moscow turned to imports to make up for falling domestic fuel production.The fuel was loaded at several South Korean ports and carried to Russia’s far east in 14 voyages by seven tankers, according to an analysis of port records and ship-tracking data by The Guardian. Three of the vessels were under UK and European Union sanctions.One sanctioned tanker received about 26,000 tonnes of fuel from another vessel in a ship-to-ship transfer in South Korean waters. Such transfers can make cargo origins harder to trace and allow ships to avoid port terminals.The largest carrier was the sanctioned Layla, which made two trips from Ulsan in south-eastern South Korea to Vladivostok on 19 July and 10 August, carrying 57,000 tonnes of diesel in total.On its first trip, Layla told South Korean authorities it was heading to Vladivostok. On the second, it declared Niigata in Japan as its destination before sailing to Vladivostok.The Russian-flagged Astoria, also under Australian sanctions, loaded nearly 11,000 tonnes of fuel at Ulsan on 1 August.It declared Japan as its destination before sailing to Vladivostok.The third sanctioned tanker, Chongchon, did not berth at a port. Instead, it took on about 26,000 tonnes of fuel from the unsanctioned Celeste I at an anchorage off Yeosu in southern South Korea in early August. It then sailed to Vladivostok after declaring Singapore as its destination.The owners and managers of the four tankers did not respond to requests for comment. South Korean port records do not show who owned or sold the fuel.The shipments come as Ukrainian drone strikes disrupt Russia’s oil-refining capacity.The International Energy Agency said Russian refinery throughput fell in June to its lowest level in more than 20 years. Diesel production was nearly 30% lower than a year earlier.Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, the HUR, has said Moscow has been forced to import fuel products to feed the “Russian war machine”.Russia imported 368,000 tonnes of oil products by sea in August, according to Kpler data analysed by CREA. That was more than seven times the previous month and the highest monthly total since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.South Korea supplied 112,000 tonnes, or 31%, of the total, second only to India.Kpler data showed that buyers included Rosneft, Russia’s state-controlled oil company, which is under UK, US, EU and Australian sanctions. NNK, a Russian oil group, was also among the buyers. Its owner, Eduard Khudainatov, and NNK-Oil are under UK sanctions.South Korea balances Ukraine support with Russia tiesThe fuel trade comes despite South Korea’s support for Ukraine. Seoul has provided humanitarian aid and non-lethal military supplies, including helmets, body armour and demining vehicles. In 2023, it pledged $2.3bn in support, most of it in loans.President Lee Jae Myung also pledged $100m for Ukraine’s reconstruction at a Nato summit in Turkey.But Seoul has also sought to maintain ties with Russia. Throughout the war, it has ruled out sending weapons directly to Ukraine, in line with its policy of not supplying lethal arms to countries at war.Moscow has also shown interest in restoring relations with South Korea, including trade ties.The fuel shipments involve vessels sanctioned by some of South Korea’s western partners but do not appear to breach South Korean law. Seoul’s measures against Russia mainly focus on export controls covering goods such as industrial machinery, electronics and vehicles.The shipments come as relations between Seoul and Kyiv face strain over the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea, which Seoul has said was meant to remain secret.Seoul defends its export controlsFuel loadings at South Korean ports began to rise sharply in July, around the time Lee pledged $100m for Ukraine’s reconstruction.A 2025 trade association survey found that nearly 80% of South Korean companies that had stopped exporting to Russia since the war began were open to restarting trade.In March, South Korea capped exports of certain fuels and imported Russian naphtha under a US sanctions waiver after the war with Iran shut the Strait of Hormuz.On 1 October, the UK temporarily exempted South Korea’s existing gas contracts from a ban on maritime services for Russian LNG, which will take effect in January 2027.South Korea’s foreign ministry did not directly address the shipments or the sanctioned tankers. In a statement, it said that as “a responsible member of the international community, the government supports, and is actively taking part in, international efforts to help end the war in Ukraine and bring about a peaceful recovery.”The ministry said that it had expanded export controls on Russia under the Foreign Trade Act “beyond strategic items to 1,402 non-strategic items with a high potential for diversion to military use” and was “strictly enforcing” them.The government “continues to monitor the implementation of its export controls on Russia and, where necessary, takes action in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations,” the ministry said.
Article Summary: More than 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mainly diesel, was shipped from South Korea to Russia. Moscow turned to imports to make up for falling domestic fuel production. Fuel was loaded at several South Korean ports and carried to Russia’s far east in 14 voyages by seven tankers. Three of the vessels were under UK and EU sanctions.

Article Title: Google nears $1 billion-plus nuclear power deal with Constellation amid AI boom
Article Text:
Google to seal $1 billion-plus nuclear power

Why tech cos are turning to nuclear power?

Google is close to striking a deal to buy nuclear power from Constellation Energy Corp, for its data centres, as tech gaints look for more reliable electricity to support the rapid growth of artificial intelligence.The Alphabet Inc. company could pay $1 billion or more under a multi-year agreement with Constellation, according to people familiar with the talks, as cited by Bloomberg. The deal could be announced as soon as this week. The people asked not to be named because the discussions are private.The possible deal would add to the company's already existing agreements with nuclear power companies. Last year, Google agreed to buy electricity from NextEra Energy Inc. The deal will support the company's plans to restart the Duane Arnold reactor in Iowa, which has been shut since 2020.Google also reached an agreement with Southern Co. last month for new nuclear capacity by funding upgrades at two nuclear plants. The tech firm's talks with Constellation come as technology companies face rising electricity needs from the artificial intelligence boom and growing data-centre demand.Nuclear power can provide electricity around the clock and does not produce emissions. Recent deals have mainly focused on existing nuclear plants because building new reactors can take a decade or more, including the time needed for permits and construction.The next generation of nuclear technology is also still expected to be years away from being widely deployed.Amazon.com Inc. agreed last week to buy 690 megawatts of power from Constellation. The deal includes capacity from an upgrade to the Calvert Cliffs nuclear facility in Maryland, Bloomberg reported.Microsoft Corp. agreed in 2024 to buy power from the shut Three Mile Island nuclear plant in Pennsylvania, where Constellation is planning to restart the reactor by next year.Nuclear energy has gained interest again in recent years after safety concerns and high costs reduced interest in it earlier last decade.Growing demand for electricity from data centres has also increased interest in nuclear power. Apart from companies, many countries are also turning to nuclear energy to meet rising power demand while reducing emissions.
Article Summary: Google is close to striking a deal to buy nuclear power from Constellation Energy Corp, for its data centres. The company could pay $1 billion or more under a multi-year agreement with Constellation, according to people familiar with the talks. The deal could be announced as soon as this week.

Article Title: Oil prices hover near $100 as Middle East supply holds up, Gulf risks persist
Article Text:
Houthi attacks keep Gulf supply risks alive

Supply squeeze could last

Demand recovery may take longer

Oil prices remained close to $100 a barrel on Tuesday, with steady Middle Eastern oil exports helping to ease supply concerns. However, continued attacks in the region kept traders alert to the risk of disruptions to Gulf supplies.Brent crude was trading at $100.6 a barrel, up 24 cents or 0.24%, while WTI stood at $89.60, gaining 17 cents or 0.19%.The benchmarks have eased from around $103 a barrel after shipping data showed Middle Eastern crude exports had exceeded pre-war levels on four days in the final week of September. Oil shipments held up despite attacks on vessels travelling through the Strait of Hormuz.The supply picture also improved after G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves. The group also pledged not to restrict energy exports following pressure from US President Donald Trump.But the stronger oil flows have not removed concerns about future supplies, with fresh attacks adding to uncertainty over Gulf shipments.Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said on Monday that they had attacked several sites in Saudi Arabia, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh and Abha airport.Saudi Arabia had not immediately confirmed the attacks.The attacks came as US-Iran talks remained at a stalemate, while the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi forces continued to raise concerns about possible disruptions to supplies from Saudi Arabia, the region's largest oil exporter."Without a clear diplomatic breakthrough or a further material improvement in export efficiency, the floor under prices looks reasonably firm," Waterer said.The concerns around supply could persist well beyond the immediate crisis. Oil industry executives at a conference in London on Monday said shipping bottlenecks, deep cuts in refinery output and inventory withdrawals that could take years to replace could keep global oil prices high beyond this year.The Strait of Hormuz has been a major source of disruption since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran at the end of February, when Iran effectively closed the waterway and choked exports through the crucial shipping route.The disruption has been compounded by attacks on oil and gas infrastructure, which have hampered production and affected exports of crude oil and refined fuels."I think it is going to be bedlam for the bulk of the end of the year and maybe 2027," Petronas CEO Tengku Muhammad Taufik said.Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser said it could take up to two years to rebuild global oil stockpiles that have been drawn down as an emergency measure.Speaking at the Energy Intelligence Forum in London in his first conference address since the start of the Iran war, Nasser said the scale of the stockpile withdrawals would make replenishment a long process."Until Hormuz fully re-opens and confidence returns, the crude reality is that pressure at both ends of the barrel will intensify. Even then, replenishing inventories while meeting demand could take up to two years," he said.Nasser said 3 billion barrels had been lost since the start of the conflict, while 1 billion barrels had been withdrawn from global inventories. The reference to both ends of the barrel covers unrefined crude as well as refined products such as diesel and jet fuel.The supply disruption could also affect the timeline for a recovery in global oil demand.ConocoPhillips Executive Chair Ryan Lance said demand could take until 2028 or 2029 to recover from this year's decline, although he expects it to grow after that.Lance said the floor for US benchmark WTI crude would rise to around $70 a barrel, with a mid-cycle price of $65 to $70 a barrel.US oil production could exceed 14 million to 14.5 million barrels per day if prices remain strong, he said, although he did not specify what he meant by strong prices.Brent futures had traded just above $100 a barrel on Monday, while WTI was close to $90, keeping both benchmarks elevated as traders balanced stronger Middle Eastern exports against the continuing risk of supply disruptions.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $100.6 a barrel, up 24 cents or 0.24%, while WTI stood at $89.60. The benchmarks have eased from around $103 a barrel after shipping data showed Middle Eastern crude exports had exceeded pre-war levels on four days in the final week of September.

Article Title: Trump signs order to ease diesel costs, ‘save millions of dollars’ for farmers
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump

Diesel still costs well above last year

Trump drops diesel export ban

US President Donald Trump on Monday (local time) signed an executive order aimed to ease the burden of high diesel prices on farmers, truckers and other businesses, as fuel costs continue to put pressure on Republicans ahead of the November midterm elections.Trump announced the move during a campaign stop in Grand Island, Nebraska, saying that loosening limits on the tax-free use of red-dyed diesel would save farmers “millions” and help bring down the cost of goods and groceries.“Pete and Jim, this should absolutely ensure your election, I guarantee you that,” Trump said, addressing Republican governor Pete Ricketts and governor Jim Pillen.The order directs states to increase the availability of tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is used in farming, construction and other industries. It also calls on states to consider waiving certain fuel taxes and includes so-called non-enforcement of dyed diesel limitations.Red-dyed diesel is exempt from federal and state excise taxes. The administration says that temporarily easing restrictions would reduce costs for businesses that depend on diesel.“The typical trucker will save more than $100 every time they fill up,” Trump said as he signed the order before a crowd in Grand Island.“Farmers will also save millions and millions of dollars, and this order will also drive down the cost of all goods and to go to grocery prices very substantially.”The steps also include the treasury department reviewing certain taxes on diesel.Ten states accounting for roughly a third of US diesel sales had already taken steps to allow wider use of dyed diesel by Friday, according to research firm ClearView Energy Partners, cited by Politico. Several states had also waived taxes on diesel used in agricultural vehicles.The move comes as diesel prices remain sharply higher than a year ago.The average price of diesel fell to $6.32 a gallon on Monday, down 13 cents from the previous week but still $2.63 higher than a year ago, according to AAA.Fuel prices have surged amid the ongoing war against Iran and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. The conflicts have contributed to a significant decline in the amount of diesel available on the global market.Exports of American diesel have also risen to record levels since the US and Israel launched a war with Iran in February and Ukraine began targeting Russian refineries.The red-dyed diesel measure follows weeks of uncertainty over how the administration would respond to rising fuel prices.Trump had repeatedly backed an outright ban on diesel exports as agriculture-state Republicans, including Iowa Senator Chuck Grassley, pushed for action to lower costs for farmers.Energy secretary Chris Wright and White House energy advisers had been working on alternatives.But on Friday, Trump ruled out a diesel export ban and said he had never really considered one, after Europe agreed to release fuel from its diesel reserves.Agriculture secretary Brooke Rollins said Monday morning that Trump would announce additional short-term relief for farmers in Nebraska and that she would also discuss the issue during a stop in Iowa.High fuel and grocery prices have become a major concern for rural voters, many of whom have backed Trump and Republicans in recent elections. Nebraska farmers and ranchers have also been angered by the administration's plan to allow more imports of foreign beef.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order aimed to ease the burden of high diesel prices on farmers, truckers and other businesses. The order directs states to increase the availability of tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, which is used in farming, construction and other industries. It also calls on states to consider waiving certain fuel taxes.

Article Title: Saudi oil under fire, Aramco plots new routes to keep barrels flowing
Article Text:
Smoke rises from a fire at the Aramco refinery south of Riyadh (Reuters)

Saudi Aramco is working on new oil export routes and overseas storage as repeated attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and tankers expose vulnerabilities in the kingdom’s crude supply network.According to Reuters, Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said the company is working on a fourth and fifth export route and studying additional overseas storage to help deal with short-term disruptions.He said Aramco is currently meeting all customer requirements and can make 12 million barrels per day available within days if needed."We start repairing assets while they are still on fire," Nasser said, describing Aramco’s approach to damaged infrastructure.Nasser said Aramco continues to export crude through Yanbu as well as Egypt’s Sidi Kerir and Port Said, while also relying heavily on ship-to-ship transfers to keep supplies moving.Looking beyond the immediate oil supply disruptions, Nasser also outlined Aramco's longer term plans for natural gas. He said the company expects to produce around 9 million barrels of oil equivalent per day of natural gas by 2040.The comments come amid escalating attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping.The attacks have raised concerns over the security of Saudi Arabia’s oil export network, particularly after disruptions to the East-West pipeline, a key route that allows the kingdom to move crude towards the Red Sea and bypass the Strait of Hormuz.Nasser also warned that commercially available information is making energy infrastructure easier to track and target."Open data such as satellite imagery and shipping logs are increasingly being weaponised against infrastructure and tankers," he said.Despite the attacks, Nasser said Aramco has not needed to tap its strategic product reserves and has enough inventory within its system to continue supplying customers.But the disruption is already creating a significant premium in the physical oil market. Nasser said physical barrels are sometimes trading $20 to $50 per barrel above the Brent benchmark, highlighting the rising cost of securing and transporting crude.The Aramco CEO also warned that the impact of the disruption could persist even after immediate supply routes stabilise. He said the world needs at least 2 million barrels per day of additional demand for the next 18 months to rebuild current oil inventories.Looking beyond the immediate oil disruption, Nasser also outlined Aramco's long-term gas ambitions, saying the company expects to produce around 9 million barrels of oil equivalent per day of natural gas by 2040.The 2040 target is part of Aramco's longer term strategy, separate from the immediate security challenges facing its oil export network.
Article Summary: Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said the company is working on a fourth and fifth export route and studying additional overseas storage. He said Aramco is currently meeting all customer requirements and can make 12 million barrels per day available within days if needed. Nasser also outlined Aramco's longer term plans for natural gas.

Article Title: Japan's Nikkei jumps 2.5% above 70,000 to three-month high as AI stocks rally
Article Text:
Japan's Nikkei rises to three month-high

Wall Street gains lift Japan stocks

30-year bond yield hits record high

What is keeping bond market under pressure

Japan’s Nikkei got an AI-powered boost on Monday, jumping over 2% to cross 70,000 for the first time in three months. Benchmark index Nikkei climbed 2.53% to 70,037.61 by the midday break, while the broader Topix gained 1.16% to 4,138.57.Chip-related companies emerged as the biggest drivers of Nikkei's rise. Tokyo Electron gained 5.7% and Advantest rose 4.5%, while technology investor SoftBank Group advanced 3.68%.Memory maker Kioxia, however, rose only 0.49%. Its shares remain nearly 50% below the record high reached in mid-June."Investors scooped up AI-related stocks, but the market sentiment is muted compared with earlier this year when the Nikkei hit a record high," said Mamoru Shimode, chief strategist at Resona Asset Management. The AI rally will continue, but the markets will be more selective."Shimode said Kioxia’s limited gains could reflect selling by investors who had suffered losses in the stock."Investors probably tried to buy Kioxia shares on the rise, but at the same time others who have losses in the shares sold stocks on a rally, which is why their gains are limited," Shimode said.The advance in Japanese equities followed a rise in US stocks on Friday.Weaker-than-expected jobs data reduced expectations for a rate hike by the Federal Reserve at its policy meeting this month.Japanese financial stocks also moved higher. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group rose 0.99%, while Mizuho Financial Group gained 1.86%.Within the Topix, the growth share index climbed 1.46%, compared with a 0.89% rise in the value share index.The gains were mixed across the broader market. Of more than 1,500 stocks on the Tokyo Stock Exchange’s prime market, 53% rose, 42% declined and 3% were unchanged.While equities rallied, Japan’s bond market came under pressure, with the 30-year government bond yield climbing to a record 4.235%. The move came as investors awaited Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s policy speech later on Monday, which is being closely watched for clues on the government’s policy stance.Investors were awaiting Takaichi’s remarks at the opening of an extraordinary parliamentary session. Her policy speech is being closely watched after local media reported that she was expected to pledge a nimble response to unexpected developments in the economy and financial markets.Markets are also scrutinising her comments for signs of a possible shift in her reflationary policy stance, following US pressure to stem the yen’s weakness."The yields across the curve stand at this level based on expectations for a shift in Takaichi's policy, but if she says anything that could suggest she would keep her expansionary policy unchanged, that could send the bond yields higher," said Masahito Sugawara, a senior strategist at Daiwa Securities.Investors have become increasingly concerned that Takaichi’s ambitious spending plans could worsen Japan’s fiscal position. She took office a year ago, and the concerns have added pressure to the government bond market.The move was concentrated in longer-dated debt, while shorter-dated yields fell. The two-year JGB yield declined 1.5 basis points to 1.9%, while the 10-year bond yield dropped 2 basis points to 3.08%.The pressure on Japanese government bonds comes amid a broader sell-off in global government debt. Elevated energy prices, persistent inflation concerns and expectations of higher interest rates have pushed yields higher across global markets.US Treasury yields also reversed earlier declines over the weekend as investors assessed the weaker-than-expected September jobs report. The data tempered expectations for further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
Article Summary: Chip-related companies emerged as the biggest drivers of Nikkei's rise. The advance in Japanese equities followed a rise in US stocks on Friday. Japan’s bond market came under pressure, with the 30-year government bond yield climbing to a record 4.235%.

Article Title: Oil prices ease slightly as G7 and Middle East crude supplies set to hit market
Article Text:
Crude prices ease marginally on Monday

Oil prices found marginal relief on Monday as concerns over global energy supplies eased with more crude entering the market. Additional shipments from the Middle East, along with the Group of Seven’s decision to release oil from emergency reserves, helped offset concerns over possible further damage to energy infrastructure in the Gulf amid the Iran war.As of 7:15 am IST, Brent Crude was down 0.54% at $101.70 while WTI Crude fell 0.92% to $90.27.The G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency stocks came last week, following pressure from US President Donald Trump. The countries also pledged not to impose energy export restrictions.The G7 move comes as Middle Eastern crude exports have already picked up. Shipping data showed that exports were above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the final week of September, despite attacks on vessels travelling through the Strait of Hormuz.The market remains exposed to developments around the Gulf.The Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia, saying the attacks were in response to 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen over the previous 12 hours.Yemen's Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said on Sunday that it was beginning a major military campaign to retake all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis.Aramco has also unexpectedly reduced its November crude oil prices for Asia to six-year lows, Reuters reported.Meanwhile, OPEC+ has postponed a review that was expected to determine oil output quotas for its members in 2027. Two sources close to the matter said the US-Israeli war on Iran had disrupted projects intended to expand production capacity across the Middle East, making estimates of future production potential uncertain.Developments in Europe are also shaping oil markets.
